headline_marked: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir [[elected as Bangladesh's 24th president]]
headline: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir elected as Bangladesh's 24th president
summary: The BNP candidate secured 255 votes in the National Parliament, defeating opponent Oli Ahmed, who received 88 votes.
details: BNP candidate Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been elected as the 24th President of Bangladesh. He secured 255 votes in a parliamentary vote, defeating his opponent, Oli Ahmed of the 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami, who received 88 votes.
The election took place on Thursday in the National Parliament. Out of 349 total voters (MPs), 343 cast their votes, while six members remained absent.

Following the announcement of the results, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman congratulated the new president-elect with a red rose. The event was marked by a spirit of cooperation, with Mirza Fakhrul shaking hands and embracing members of both the government and opposition parties.
The Election Commission has issued a gazette notification declaring Mirza Fakhrul the winner. He is scheduled to take his oath of office on Friday evening.
The transition follows the resignation of President Mohammed Sahabuddin on July 24 due to health reasons, after which Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed served as acting president.

International congratulations have already poured in from the United Kingdom and China, while domestic leaders including Professor Yunus and the Home Minister have hailed the election as a new beginning for democracy.
caption:
Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is the new President of Bangladesh! 🇧🇩

The election took place on Thursday in the National Parliament. Out of 349 total voters (MPs), 343 cast their votes, while six members remained absent.

Following the announcement of the results, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman congratulated the new president-elect with a red rose. The event was marked by a spirit of cooperation, with Mirza Fakhrul shaking hands and embracing members of both the government and opposition parties.

The Election Commission has issued a gazette notification declaring Mirza Fakhrul the winner. He is scheduled to take his oath of office on Friday evening.

The transition follows the resignation of President Mohammed Sahabuddin on July 24 due to health reasons, after which Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed served as acting president.

International congratulations have already poured in from the United Kingdom and China, while domestic leaders including Professor Yunus and the Home Minister have hailed the election as a new beginning for democracy.

headline_marked: Ruhul Kabir Rizvi [[appointed BNP acting secretary general]]
headline: Ruhul Kabir Rizvi appointed BNP acting secretary general
summary: The appointment follows Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir's election as president and comes just five days after Rizvi was inducted into the National Standing Committee.
details: BNP Standing Committee member Ruhul Kabir Rizvi has been appointed the party's acting secretary general. The decision was announced in a press release yesterday shortly after presidential election formalities were completed at the Jatiya Sangsad.
Rizvi's appointment comes five days after he was inducted into the BNP's highest policymaking body, the National Standing Committee on August 15.
He has served as the party's senior joint secretary general since 2016 and was later appointed as an adviser to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman with the rank of a minister.

Born in Kurigram, Rizvi began his political career with the left-wing Biplobi Chhatra Union and later joined Chhatra Dal, where he rose to become the first elected president of its central committee in 1992.
Rizvi is known for his prominence during the party's years under the previous government's rule, remaining at the party's Nayapaltan headquarters to brief the media.
According to party leaders, over 180 cases were filed against him during that period of political tension.
caption:
From student leader to acting secretary general: Ruhul Kabir Rizvi takes over a key leadership role in the BNP.

BNP Standing Committee member Ruhul Kabir Rizvi has been appointed the party's acting secretary general. The decision was announced in a press release yesterday shortly after presidential election formalities were completed at the Jatiya Sangsad.

Rizvi's appointment comes five days after he was inducted into the BNP's highest policymaking body, the National Standing Committee on August 15.

He has served as the party's senior joint secretary general since 2016 and was later appointed as an adviser to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman with the rank of a minister.

Born in Kurigram, Rizvi began his political career with the left-wing Biplobi Chhatra Union and later joined Chhatra Dal, where he rose to become the first elected president of its central committee in 1992.

Rizvi is known for his prominence during the party's years under the previous government's rule, remaining at the party's Nayapaltan headquarters to brief the media.

According to party leaders, over 180 cases were filed against him during that period of political tension.
